title: How to Build Conditional Workflows in Process Management
summary: Learn to build conditional workflows in process management, showing fields, buttons, and steps only when they matter, no code needed.
body_markdown:
Building **conditional workflows in process management** means showing fields, buttons, and steps only when they make sense at that point in the process, instead of leaving the card full of irrelevant information. In **Jestor** , this is set up through conditionals, with no programming required.


Tools locked into a simple board-and-card model tend to force the team to see the same fields and buttons at every stage of the process, even when they don't apply there.


That clutters the card, raises the risk of error (like approving at the wrong stage), and makes it hard to see what actually matters at each step.


## Where a Lack of Conditionals Usually Gets in the Way


- Cards show information from every stage at once, even the stages that don't apply at that moment
- Action buttons appear at stages where they shouldn't, raising the risk of error
- The team has to visually hunt for the right information among fields that don't matter there
- Business rules with exceptions end up handled through parallel processes, outside the main tool


## How to Set Up Conditionals in the Process


1. Identify which fields or buttons only make sense at specific stages of the process
2. Set the conditional by stage: what shows on the card's cover changes automatically
3. Define conditionals by field value, not just by stage (for example, show a button only if the value is high)
4. Turn action buttons on or off depending on the stage, to prevent clicks at the wrong moment
5. Test the full workflow, moving a card through every stage, to confirm what shows up at each one


Type of conditional Example use


By stage Show value and priority only at the quoting stage


By field value Show the approval button only if the value passes a threshold


By priority Highlight extra information only for high-priority cards


## Why Jestor Handles This Well


- Conditionals apply to displayed fields, card color, and buttons, not just the process stage
- Setup works the same way as form conditionals, with no extra learning curve
- Cards stay more focused and fit more relevant information on the same screen
- No code is needed to build these rules

## Frequently asked questions


**Do conditional workflows require programming to set up?** No, conditionals are configured visually, the same way form conditionals are; see more at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Can a button be made conditional, not just a field?** Yes, buttons can also appear only in specific stages or conditions.


**Do conditionals change who has permission to edit what?** Not necessarily, conditionals are mostly about usability; permissions are set separately.


**Does this help prevent approval errors at the wrong stage?** Yes, showing the right button only at the right stage reduces that type of error.


Setting up **conditional workflows in process management** is what separates a useful card from one full of information nobody uses.
